question: MDR-TB is defined as resistance to both isoniazid and rifampicin — the two most potent first-line anti-tuberculosis drugs — and requires treatment with second-line drugs for a minimum of 18–20 months under the RNTCP/NSP guidelines.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Reconsider. The WHO and RNTCP define MDR-TB specifically as combined resistance to isoniazid AND rifampicin. This definition matters clinically because it signals the loss of the two most effective first-line drugs.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. MDR-TB is precisely defined as resistance to at least INH + RIF. Second-line regimens (bedaquiline-based under NSP 2020) are required, and treatment duration is substantially longer than for drug-sensitive TB.
